chunks: He said: And Muhammad ibn Ata al-Darghamah narrated to me from Khallad al-Lu'lu'i who said: Narrated to me Saeed al-Makki from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he had a high status with him,

He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Saeed, the Imams are twelve; when six have passed, Allah will grant ease to the seventh, and five persons from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, will be Imams, and the sun will rise from its west through the hand of the sixth.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the key eschatological signs regarding the twelve Imams mentioned in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* serves as a crucial proof for the number and identity of the Twelve Imams, specifically linking the eschatological sign of the sun rising from the west to the Sixth Imam, Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kadhim). It highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in establishing divine rule and underscores the theological significance of the seventh Imam, who brings ease after the trials of the preceding six.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 44 - Narrated to me Muhammad bin Ataa Zarghama from Khallad Lului that: Narrated to me Saeed Makki who was a close confidant of Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s); that

Imam (a.s) said: O Saeed, the Imams are twelve; when six of them pass away, Allah, the Mighty and the High would give ease to the seven of them and five persons from us, Ahle Bayt (a.s) will be Imams and through the sixth, sun would rise from the west.
